name: oud_lead
description: Arab oud: carries the tune in the passing section and a decorated counter-line later.
character: A fretless pear-shaped lute plucked with a plectrum: a warm, woody pluck whose long notes are decorated with a quick trill, answering the tune a few milliseconds behind it the way an Arab ensemble does.
sources: KB arabic (heterophony: instruments play the same melody each with its own ornaments and a micro-delay of about 12 ms; the oud trill and its plectrum pluck; the maqsum cycle)
ESTIMATE: the SoundFont nylon guitar stands in for the oud: no quarter-tone or fretless slide is available on a fixed-pitch pentatonic line
STARTING VALUE: onset_fade_ms 8: several strokes land together on every strong beat and their sharp starts add into one impulse the click row flags; a soft attack is also what "smooth" asks for

MEASURED: the mastered file had click events at the onsets of overlapping notes, where the sampler tick lands on a still-ringing note and soften_onsets leaves it alone by design; STARTING VALUE: low-pass at 6000 Hz, above what a phone speaker returns
STARTING VALUE: gate 1.0 with a 40 ms overlap: at gate 0.9 a note ended 10 % early and the stem gate found a 35 ms digital-silence hole between two plucks

STARTING VALUE: low-pass at 4.5 kHz: a phone speaker returns little above about 5 kHz (KB short-form-functional-music), and the sharp edges of plucked and struck onsets above it are what the click row reacts to
MEASURED: short_form_report found 10.5% of the master below 200 Hz and 13.9% from 200 to 300 Hz, where a phone speaker returns little; STARTING VALUE: high-pass at 220 Hz

CARRIED OVER from the ringtone project 'Confluence', where each filter, fade and level in this preset was set by a measurement (click count, stem.dropout, equal_loudness); not re-measured for the alarm until the gate runs
